cards.body:
*Lesson 4.4 · RAG: Answering From Your Documents*

_≈ 2–3 hours · with Emeka_

Models know a lot about the world and nothing about Harvest Lane's refund policy. *Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)* fixes that: before answering, the agent searches your documents, pulls out the few passages that matter, and answers from them, citing where the answer came from. Done right, it's the difference between "I think…" and "Section 2 says…".

*Your problem:* Agents guess at your policies instead of quoting them.
*The plan:* Build RAG: split documents, store them as vectors, retrieve, and cite the source.
*After this lesson:* Your agents answer from your documents and name the section.

*The 12-page PDF nobody reads*

*The policies:* Refunds, cancellations, substitutions, business accounts: 12 pages that Tolu's lawyer friend helped write.

*The mistake:* The agent promises a full refund. The policy refunds only the delivery fee for lateness.

*Why:* Both rules sat in one big chunk. The agent blended "full refund" from one with "late delivery" from the other.

*Glitch:* "Bigger chunks mean more context, and more context is always better. Right?"
*RAG in two pipelines*

*Embeddings, in plain words*

An *embeddings model* turns a piece of text into a long list of numbers that captures its _meaning_. Texts with similar meaning get similar numbers, even with different words: "my order came late" lands near "delivery arrived after the agreed window". A *vector store* (Supabase with pgvector, Pinecone, Qdrant…) stores those lists and quickly finds the ones nearest to a question's list.

- *Chunk*: A piece of a document small enough to be about one thing. You search and retrieve chunks, not whole documents.
- *Chunk size and overlap*: How long each piece is, and how much text consecutive pieces share, so a rule split across a boundary isn't lost.
- *Metadata*: Labels stored with each chunk: source file, section, version date, product. Used to filter and to cite.
- *Top-k*: How many chunks to retrieve per question (often 3–5).

*Try it: chunk size decides what the agent reads*

Below is a short version of Harvest Lane's policy. Adjust the chunking and ask a question to see which chunks would be retrieved. Start with Glitch's 1,000 characters and no overlap, then shrink.
Hands-on lab: Try it: chunk size decides what the agent reads. It's interactive, so open it in the app and try it there.

*Answer from the source, or say "I don't know"*

- *Ground the answer*: Instruct: answer only from retrieved text; name the section; if the text doesn't answer the question, say so and offer to ask a person.
- *Quote the rule*: For money and promises (refunds, cancellations), quote the exact sentence. Paraphrases drift.
- *Keep documents current*: Store a version date in metadata. When the policy changes, delete the old chunks and load the new version, or old rules come back to haunt you.
- *RAG isn't a database*: "How much are tomatoes today?" is a lookup (4.2), not a document search. RAG is for text: policies, manuals, FAQs, contracts.

*Sage:* "I don't know, but I'll ask Tolu" is a good answer. A confident wrong answer about refunds costs real money and trust. Test me with questions the documents _don't_ answer, and check I admit it.

*RAG nodes in n8n*

- *Vector store node*: (Supabase, Pinecone, Qdrant, PGVector, or the in-memory Simple Vector Store for testing). Modes include _Insert Documents_, _Get Many_, and _Retrieve Documents (As Tool for AI Agent)_, which gives the agent a search tool with a name, description and result limit.
- *Embeddings sub-node*: Choose one model (e.g. from OpenAI, Google or Cohere, or a local Ollama model) and use the *same* one for inserting and retrieving.
- *Default Data Loader*: Reads text or a binary file (such as a PDF) and attaches metadata.
- *Text splitter*: The Recursive Character Text Splitter sets chunk size and overlap, and tries to split at paragraph and sentence boundaries first.
- *Supabase setup*: Supabase needs a table and a matching function (usually `match_documents`). Copy the SQL from Supabase's LangChain guide, and set the vector size to your embeddings model's size.

cards.body:
*Solved problem: the policy assistant*

*The goal.* Load Harvest Lane's policy PDF into Supabase, then give the support agent a `search_policies` tool so it answers refund, cancellation and substitution questions with the exact section, and says "I don't know" when the policy is silent.

*Step 1 · Prepare Supabase*

In your Supabase project, open the SQL editor and run the setup from Supabase's LangChain guide: enable the `vector` extension, create the `documents` table and the `match_documents` function. Set the vector size to match your embeddings model (for example, OpenAI's `text-embedding-3-small` produces 1,536 numbers). In n8n, add a *Supabase* credential (project URL and service role key: keep it in the credential only; it bypasses row-level security).

*Step 2 · Build the loading workflow*

*HL · Load policies*: Manual Trigger → *Google Drive · Download* the policy PDF → *Supabase Vector Store · Insert Documents* (table `documents`), with sub-nodes:

- *Embeddings*: your chosen model.
- *Default Data Loader*: type Binary; metadata `source = policies-v3.pdf`, `version = 2026-10-01`.
- *Recursive Character Text Splitter*: chunk size ≈ *500*, overlap ≈ *80*. Start there and test (Card 3).

Run it once. In Supabase's table editor you should see rows with content, metadata and an embedding.

*Step 3 · Give the agent a search tool*

On your support agent, add *Supabase Vector Store* in *Retrieve Documents (As Tool for AI Agent)* mode, with the same embeddings model. Name: `search_policies`. Limit: 4. Description: _"Searches Harvest Lane's official customer policies (refunds, late delivery, cancellations, substitutions, business accounts). Use it before answering any question about what a customer is entitled to. Returns the most relevant policy passages."_
*Step 4 · Ground the answers*
Code example on screen (Ground the answers): open it in the app.

*Step 5 · Test with answerable and unanswerable questions*

_(Code on screen in the app.)_
Hands-on lab: Test with answerable and unanswerable questions. It's interactive, so open it in the app and try it there.

Expected for question 1: _"Our late-delivery policy refunds the delivery fee: 'Lateness alone does not qualify for a refund of the goods.' I've noted the delay for Tolu."_ Questions 6 and 7 must end with "I'll ask Tolu", not invented rules.

- *~500 / 80* chunk size / overlap to start from
- *4* passages retrieved per question
- *8/8* target: correct, cited, or honestly "not sure"

*Why this approach works*

- Chunks small enough to hold one rule stop policies blending.
- Overlap keeps rules that cross a boundary intact.
- The same embeddings model for loading and searching keeps the search meaningful.
- Quoting and naming sections makes answers checkable.
- "I'm not sure" is an allowed, tested answer.

*Common mistakes to avoid*

- Huge chunks "for more context".
- Different embeddings models for loading and searching.
- Loading v4 of the policy without deleting v3's chunks.
- Using RAG for live data like prices (use a lookup tool).
- Testing only questions the document answers.

*Glitch hunt*

*Glitch:* Five ways to make a smart agent read the wrong page.

*A:* Answers mix the damaged-produce refund with the late-delivery rule.
*B:* Search returns nonsense for every question after Tolu "upgraded the embeddings model" in the agent.
*C:* The agent quotes the old 24-hour cancellation rule, which changed last month.
*D:* Asked "do you deliver to Abuja?", the agent says yes, confidently.
*E:* A rule split across two chunks comes back half-finished: "…are charged 50% of".

cards.prompt: Made your call on each one? Tap Reveal to check.
cards.answer:
*A:* chunks too big, so both rules land in one chunk. Shrink the chunk size (or split on headings) and re-load.
*B:* the agent's embeddings model no longer matches the one used for loading. Use the same model, or re-load everything with the new one.
*C:* old version chunks are still in the store. Delete by the `version` or `source` metadata before loading the new version.
*D:* no "I don't know" rule, and the model filled the gap. Instruct it to answer only from passages, and test unanswerable questions.
*E:* no overlap between chunks. Add overlap (about 10–20% of the chunk size).

cards.title: Bronze (+25 XP): RAG over one PDF
cards.body:
- Write a two-page policy document for Harvest Lane (or a business you know), with clear headings.
- Load it into a vector store (Supabase, or the Simple Vector Store to start) and build an agent with a search tool.
- Run the 8 test questions, adapted to your document.

*Done when:*
- At least 5 of the 6 answerable questions are correct and cite a section, and both unanswerable questions get an honest "not sure".

cards.title: Silver (+50 XP): Metadata filters
cards.body:
- Load two documents: the customer policy and a product guide (storage tips, seasons, per product).
- Add metadata: `doc_type` (policy or product) and, for product chunks, `product`.
- Give the agent two search tools, each filtered by `doc_type`, with distinct descriptions.

*Done when:*
- Policy questions never retrieve product chunks (check the execution log), and "how should I store ugu?" retrieves only ugu chunks.

cards.title: Gold (+100 XP): A RAG assistant on your own documents
cards.body:
- Choose 3–5 real documents from your work (remove anything confidential or personal).
- Load them with metadata and a versioning plan (how you'll replace a document when it changes).
- Write 15 test questions: 10 answerable, 5 not. Test three chunk sizes (e.g. 300, 600, 1,000) and record the scores.

*Done when:*
- You have a table of scores by chunk size, a chosen setting with a reason, and a written replace-a-document procedure that you've tested once.

cards.q: What does an embeddings model do?
options: Turns text into numbers that capture meaning, so similar texts can be found
cards.why: Similar meaning → nearby numbers → found by vector search.

cards.q: Answers blend two different policies. Most likely cause?
options: Chunks so big that both policies share one chunk
cards.why: Each chunk should be about one thing. Smaller chunks (or heading-based splits) fix it.

cards.q: Why must loading and searching use the same embeddings model?
options: Different models produce incompatible numbers, so search becomes meaningless
cards.why: Distances only mean something within one model's number space.

cards.q: "How much are tomatoes today?" Best approach?
options: RAG over last year's price PDFs
A lookup tool on the live price list
cards.why: RAG is for text documents; live data needs a lookup (4.2).

cards.q: The policy doesn't cover the question. The agent should…
options: Say it isn't sure and offer to ask a person
cards.why: An honest “not sure” protects money and trust. Test for it.

cards.body:
*Remember this*

1. RAG = search your documents, then answer from what you found.
2. Two pipelines: load once per version; retrieve on every question.
3. One chunk, one topic; overlap so rules aren't cut in half.
4. Same embeddings model for loading and searching.
5. Metadata for filtering, citing and versioning.
6. Answer only from passages, quote money rules, and say "not sure" when needed.
7. RAG for documents; lookup tools for live data.

*Lesson 4.4 complete!* _RAG: Answering From Your Documents_ is done and saved to your progress, on WhatsApp and in the app.

Next up: Lesson 4.5, _Guardrails & Human-in-the-Loop_.
